candidates.statement: 4 A reference listed drug “is the listed drug identified by FDA as the drug product upon which an applicant relies in seeking approval of its ANDA” (21 CFR 314.3(b)). A reference standard, which is selected by FDA, is the specific drug product that the ANDA applicant must use in conducting any in vivo bioequivalence testing required to support approval of its ANDA (see § 314.3(b)). We recommend that the reference standard also be used for in vitro testing.
candidates.context: 3 A complex product , as defined in the GDUFA Reauthorization Performance Goals and Program Enhancements Fiscal Years 2023–2027 (GDUFA III Commitment Letter) (accessible at https://www.fda.gov/media/153631/download ), includes, among others, products with complex formulations (e.g., colloids) and complex routes of delivery (e.g., locally acting drugs such as dermatological products). There may be circumstances (e.g., when the RLD is no longer marketed) in which the reference standard is a drug product other than the RLD. For more information on RLD and reference standard products, see the guidance f or industry Referencing Approved Drug Products in ANDA Submissions (October 2020). We update guidances periodically. For the most recent version of a guidance, check the FDA guidance web page at https://www.fda.gov/regulatory-information/search-fda-guidance-documents .

candidates.statement: It is conventional to evaluate different membranes during IVRT method development (all using 158 the same receptor solution); these membranes are frequently synthetic membranes used for the 159 filtration of particulate matter in solutions. IVRT membranes are selected based upon their 160 effective pore size (e.g., 0.45 micrometers (μm)), as well as their expected inertness to binding 161 the drug. Information should be provided in the IVRT method development report on each 162 membrane’s binding to the drug and its chemical compatibility with relevant receptor solution(s) 163 selected for the IVRT method (based on the preceding phase of IVRT method development), as 164 well as information on the linearity and precision of the resulting release rate when each 165 membrane is used in an IVRT, as this information can help to explain why a specific membrane 166 is optimal for the IVRT method. 167

candidates.statement: The equipment, methodologies, and study conditions used in the IVRT pivotal study should be 172 appropriately validated or qualified. It is conventional to initiate the validation of the sample 173 analytical method (e.g., a HPLC or UPLC method) for the IVRT before initiating the IVRT 174 method validation itself, although certain components of the sample analysis method validation 175 (e.g., stability) often proceed in parallel with the IVRT method validation. If an applicant elects 176 to use equipment, methodologies, or study conditions that are different from those recommended 177 in this guidance or in USP <1724>, the applicant should demonstrate why the differences are 178 scientifically justified. 14 It is important to consistently identify all relevant method parameters for 179 each set of IVRT results, making it clear that the results were obtained using the same IVRT 180 method parameters, and clarifying which sets of diffusion cells were run in parallel or separately. 181 Detailed protocols and well-controlled test procedures are recommended to ensure the precise 182 control of dosing, sampling, and other IVRT study parameters, and of potential sources of 183 experimental bias. 184

candidates.statement: The qualification of an IVRT method parameter refers to the process of defining what attributes 186 make it suitable to perform its function in the IVRT method. For example, when hourly 187 measurements of the temperature at the membrane surface (when mounted in a diffusion cell) 188 demonstrate that an IVRT equipment can maintain a membrane surface temperature in the range 189 of 32°C ± 1°C across 6 hours, the results can support a demonstration that the equipment is 190 qualified to perform its function in an IVRT method for which a method parameter is the control 191 of membrane surface temperature in the range of 32°C ± 1°C across 6 hours. While an IVRT 192 membrane surface temperature in the range of range of 32°C ± 1°C is appropriate for topical 193 products applied on the skin, for topical products applied on mucosal membranes (e.g., a vaginal 194 gel) the relevant IVRT membrane surface temperature would be 37°C ± 1°C. The validation of 195 the IVRT method should incorporate the following qualifications and controls, performed using 196 validated sample analytical procedures, as applicable. 197

candidates.statement: Membrane inertness should be evaluated in relation to membrane binding of the drug in the 231 receptor solution at a concentration relevant to the range of drug concentrations in the receptor 232 solution during the test. Determinations should be based upon a minimum of three replicate 233 membrane incubations for the IVRT duration at the relevant temperature (e.g., 6 hours at 32°C ± 234 1°C). Three replicate control incubations should be performed in parallel, without membranes, to 235 monitor for drug loss that is not associated with membrane binding. Aliquots of these solutions 236 should be collected before and after the duration of incubation, to assess any decrease in the 237 amount of drug in solution. The recovery of drug in solution is recommended to be within the 238 range of 100% ± 5% at the end of the test duration to qualify the inertness of the membrane. 239

candidates.statement: The recovery of released drug in the receptor solution should be characterized in each diffusion 295 cell as the cumulative amount of drug released into the receptor solution over the IVRT study 296 duration. This may be expressed as a percentage of the amount of drug in the applied dose 297 (which may be estimated based upon the nominal strength of the drug in the topical product and 298 the approximate mass of topical product dosed on the membrane). For example, if 1 gram (g) of 299 a topical product containing 5% drug was dosed on the membrane of each diffusion cell, the 300 amount of drug in the applied dose may be estimated to be 50 mg. If a total of 10 mg of drug 301 diffused into the receptor solution of each diffusion cell across the 6-hour duration of the IVRT, 302 it would be possible to estimate that the 50 mg dose would have been depleted by 10 mg, 303 amounting to a 20% dose depletion. The average percentage dose depletion may thereby be 304 estimated and should be reported. While steady state release kinetics can typically be assumed 305 under conditions when the dose depletion is less than 30%, for some topical products, steady 306 state release kinetics may continue to be observed at higher percentage dose depletions. The 307 IVRT method may be considered adequate despite a dose depletion of greater than 30% when 308 experimental evidence illustrates that the release rate (slope) remains suitably linear for each 309 diffusion cell when plotted versus the square root of time. 310

candidates.statement: IVRT specificity is the ability to accurately monitor the proportionality of changes in the release 338 rate as a function of drug concentration in the formulation. This proportionality may be 339 illustrated in a plot of the relationship between the formulation concentration and the average 340 IVRT release rate (slope). The specificity of the IVRT method should be calculated, plotted with 341 a linear trendline, and the linearity quantified and reported as an r 2 value. To be considered 342 suitably specific, an IVRT method should be proportionally linear in its response to differences 343 in release rates, with a minimum r 2 value ≥ 0.95 for the correlation of the formulation 344 concentration to the average IVRT release rate (slope). 345
candidates.context: IVRT specificity is a function of the proportionality of release rates across different strengths of 347 the product, some, or all of which may be formulated as small-scale laboratory batches, with 348 each strength having a slightly different formulation composition to accommodate for the 349 different amount of the active ingredient in that strength of the product. These slight formulation 350 differences across the different strengths of the product may impact the ideal proportionality of 351 release rates across the different strengths of the product. 352

candidates.statement: The altered formulation used in the assessment of supplemental selectivity should have the same 421 nominal strength as the reference topical product, and may include changes in inactive 422 ingredients, changes in inactive ingredient concentration(s), changes in the manufacturing 423 processes, or combinations thereof. However, not all variations in a formulation will necessarily 424 produce a difference in the release rate compared to the reference formulation, and if two similar 425 formulations are found to have equivalent release rates, the demonstration of supplemental 426 selectivity may be inconclusive. Therefore, applicants are encouraged to develop or select an 427 altered formulation for the demonstration of supplemental selectivity based on differences in 428 physicochemical and structural properties of the formulation (relative to the reference 429 formulation) that are likely to alter the release rate of the active ingredient from the formulation. 430 The altered formulation may be a marketed topical product, such as a different dosage form at 431 the same strength of the same drug (e.g., a 5% gel versus a 5% ointment). Product batch 432 information for all topical product lots used in IVRT method development, and validation 433 studies, as applicable, should be submitted in the study reports. The topical product information 434 should include, but not be limited to, information about the batch formula, manufacturing date, 435 batch size, altered manufacturing processes (if applicable) and, if available, potency and content 436 uniformity. 437

candidates.statement: While exploratory studies performed during IVRT method development may use an unvalidated 454 sample analytical method, it is essential that all studies conducted as part of the IVRT method 455 validation use a validated sample analytical method. A validated IVRT method should use a 456 validated receptor solution sample analytical method. Therefore, a discussion of the sample 457 analytical method for the IVRT method is included in this guidance under this section. 458
